rules.reason: The Constitution is the highest authority in the repository. It is amended only through an RFC, a version bump and an ADR — never edited directly.
The ADR log is append-only and immutable (ADR-0000). A decision that proves wrong is superseded by a new ADR, never rewritten. Only new files and supersession metadata should change here.
These are the mechanisms that make the Constitution executable. Weakening a check is indistinguishable from weakening the principle it enforces.
Directory contract front matter is binding, and from M2 it generates the import-boundary configuration. Changing a contract changes what the build permits.
High-risk changes to domain and application code require approval.
High-risk changes to deployment topology require approval.
Secret-like files are blocked by policy. Private institution credentials never share a trust boundary with the public core.
